summary: Robotaxis are the one transport innovation with real scale: Waymo raised $16 billion at a $126 billion value and runs over 500,000 paid rides a week in 14 cities. Autonomous trucks, air taxis and drone delivery are funded but still pre revenue or tiny, and each waits on a regulator or a first fleet. In batteries, US EV demand fell after tax credits ended, so new cell capacity is shifting to cheaper LFP and grid storage.

innovations.name: Robotaxis
innovations.what: Cars with no driver that carry paying passengers on demand in a city.
innovations.stage_why: Paid driverless service runs at real scale in many US cities, but it is still a tiny share of all rides. Waymo did about 15 million paid rides in 2025 and is above 500,000 a week in 2026.

evidence.approvals: Waymo began paid service in Denver, San Diego and Tampa on September 1, 2026, reaching 14 US cities. Tesla opened paid Cybercab rides (no steering wheel) to the public in Austin on September 4, 2026. Zoox began testing in Houston and San Diego.
evidence.money: Waymo raised $16 billion at a $126 billion valuation (February 2, 2026), led by Dragoneer, DST and Sequoia. Tesla capex for 2026 is above $25 billion, partly for robotaxi.
evidence.revenue: Waymo did about 15 million paid rides in 2025, nearly 3x 2024, and over 500,000 paid rides a week by September 2026 with a fleet above 4,000 vehicles; its target is 1 million a week by end of 2026.

spreads_to.use: Lower crash rates shift auto insurance pricing and fleet coverage.
Less parking demand in dense cities over time.
Same driver stack moves into delivery vans and trucks.

innovations.bottleneck: City by city permits plus a proven safety record, and the AI compute and sensors (Nvidia chips, lidar from Hesai and others) inside each car. Waymo holds the lead in driverless miles.

next_milestone.event: Waymo hitting 1 million paid rides a week; Tesla Cybercab expanding beyond Austin

innovations.thesis_broken_if: A serious robotaxi crash leads to a permit pull in a major city, or Waymo stalls well short of 1 million weekly rides.

innovations.name: Autonomous trucking
innovations.what: Semi trucks that drive themselves on highways or private haul roads, sold as a per mile service to shippers and carriers.
innovations.stage_why: Driverless trucks run paid freight, but fleets are tens of trucks and revenue is a few million dollars a quarter. Aurora guides only $14 to $16 million of 2026 revenue against a $270 million quarterly loss.

evidence.approvals: Texas allows driverless trucks on public roads; Aurora runs Dallas to Houston and beyond without a driver. Kodiak runs on private Permian Basin roads for Atlas Energy.
evidence.money: Aurora had about $1.2 billion of cash at Q2 2026; Kodiak had $151.1 million. Kodiak was picked for Phase II of the Defense Innovation Unit ROADS program.
evidence.revenue: Aurora Q2 2026 revenue $2 million, about 440,000 driverless miles, aiming for over 200 driverless trucks and an $80 million run rate by end of 2026. Kodiak Q2 2026 revenue $3.5 million, 35 driverless trucks, over 20,000 loads delivered.

spreads_to.use: Frac sand hauling in the Permian (Kodiak with Atlas).
Off road haulage, such as Kodiak's West Fraser pilot in Canada.

innovations.bottleneck: Redundant truck platforms built for autonomy (steering, braking, power) from a few OEMs such as Paccar, Volvo and International, plus state laws that allow no driver. Truck build rates, not software, limit the 2026 ramp.

next_milestone.event: Aurora exiting 2026 with 200 plus driverless trucks; Kodiak long haul driverless launch

innovations.thesis_broken_if: Aurora misses its 200 truck year end target by a wide margin or a fatal driverless truck crash triggers state bans.

innovations.name: Electric air taxis (eVTOL)
innovations.what: Battery powered aircraft that take off and land vertically, carrying a pilot and four passengers on short city hops.
innovations.stage_why: No eVTOL has full FAA type certification yet. Joby is in the final Type Inspection Authorization stage and both Joby and Archer target first passenger service in the UAE in 2026, plus limited US flying under a White House pilot program.

evidence.approvals: Joby entered FAA Type Inspection Authorization with its first conforming aircraft flying in March 2026. Joby holds a 6 year exclusive to operate air taxis in Dubai. Archer targets Abu Dhabi under UAE rules, not FAA. Both are in the eVTOL Integration Pilot Program (eIPP), which allows some US operations before certification. Whether Dubai passenger service has started is unverified.
evidence.money: Joby had $1.4 billion of cash at end 2025 plus a net $1.2 billion raised in February 2026. Beta Technologies raised over $1 billion in its November 2025 IPO at $34. Eve raised $230 million.
evidence.revenue: Almost none. Beta Q1 2026 revenue was $10.1 million with a $122.3 million net loss. Eve has letters of intent for about 2,800 aircraft, which are not firm orders.

spreads_to.use: Hybrid and electric VTOL for logistics and special operations.
Organ and medical cargo flights (Beta's early use).
Airport shuttles for premium passengers (Delta with Joby, United with Archer).

innovations.bottleneck: FAA type and production certification, which only the FAA grants, plus high power aviation batteries and vertiport sites with grid power.

next_milestone.event: First paying passenger flights in Dubai (Joby) and Abu Dhabi (Archer); first eIPP flights in the US

innovations.thesis_broken_if: UAE passenger launches slip into 2027 and Joby does not receive FAA type certification by end of 2027.

innovations.name: Cheaper battery chemistries and US cell plants
innovations.what: New and cheaper battery types for EVs and grid storage: LFP (iron phosphate), sodium ion (no lithium) and solid state (more range, still in the lab).
innovations.stage_why: LFP is already mass market in China and is now being built in the US; sodium ion enters mass production at CATL in 2026; solid state is still pilot lines. US EV demand fell after the federal credit ended, so new US cells are going to grid storage.

evidence.cost: BNEF: average pack price fell 8% to a record $108 per kWh in 2025; LFP packs averaged $81 per kWh, NMC $128, and stationary storage packs $70 (down 45%).
evidence.approvals: US EV tax credit expired after September 2025. BEV share fell from a record 12% in September 2025 to about 6% to 7% in 2026, while hybrids hit a record 16% in Q2 2026.
evidence.money: Ford is building a $3.5 billion LFP plant in Marshall, Michigan using CATL licensed technology. LG Energy Solution's $5.5 billion Arizona complex includes an LFP storage cell plant starting 2026; it targets over 60 GWh of storage cells by end 2026. PowerCo (VW) is putting another $131 million into QuantumScape.
evidence.revenue: LG Energy Solution storage backlog was 140 GWh at end 2025. QuantumScape and Solid Power have no product revenue; Solid Power Q1 2026 revenue plus grants was $3.1 million.

spreads_to.use: Grid batteries for AI data center power and peak shaving; the fastest growing use.
Small high power packs for humanoids, drones and eVTOL.
Batteries for drones and soldier power, where China supply is restricted.

innovations.bottleneck: Cathode materials, graphite anodes and cell know how, mostly controlled by China (CATL, BYD) and Korean makers; US plants depend on CATL licenses and Chinese equipment.

next_milestone.event: CATL sodium ion mass production; Solid Power continuous pilot line startup; QuantumScape Eagle Line sample cells to VW

innovations.thesis_broken_if: US storage orders slow along with EVs, leaving the new LFP plants underused in 2027.

innovations.name: Drone delivery
innovations.what: Small autonomous drones that fly groceries, meals and medical supplies from a store or hub to a home in minutes.
innovations.stage_why: Paid service runs in several US metros and Walmart is scaling it to hundreds of stores, but it still needs case by case FAA waivers. The general beyond visual line of sight rule (Part 108) has been stuck at the White House since July 10, 2026.

evidence.approvals: FAA Part 108 BVLOS rule is unpublished and was sent to White House review July 10, 2026, five months past its February deadline; the FAA hopes to publish by end of 2026. Operators fly under individual waivers today.
evidence.money: Zipline raised over $600 million at a $7.6 billion valuation (January 2026) and is in talks to raise $1 billion at about $20 billion (September 2026). Walmart and Wing are adding 150 stores in 2026, aiming for over 270 sites serving about 40 million people by 2027.
evidence.revenue: Zipline passed 2.5 million commercial deliveries in the first half of 2026. Walmart has completed over 150,000 drone deliveries. Wing says total deliveries tripled in six months.

spreads_to.use: Blood, lab samples and prescriptions to hospitals and homes (Zipline's origin).
Hot food delivery through DoorDash and Wing.
Same airframes and parts makers supply military resupply drones.

innovations.bottleneck: FAA permission to fly beyond sight at scale (Part 108), plus US made motors, batteries and cameras, since federal rules push out Chinese drone parts.

next_milestone.event: FAA publishes final Part 108 BVLOS rule

innovations.thesis_broken_if: Part 108 slips deep into 2027 or Walmart pauses its store rollout.
